extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners (Licensing & Review) handling secrecy orders, foreign filing, and export-control issues
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for handling patent applications subject to Secrecy Orders or national-security markings and for obtaining/using foreign-filing licenses (including petitions and retroactive licenses). Targets compliance with 35 U.S.C. chapters and 37 CFR parts 5.11–5.25 and related export-control rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper or inadvertent disclosure reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If any significant part of the subject matter or material information relevant to the application has been revealed to any U.S. citizen in the United States, the principals must promptly inform such person of the Secrecy Order and the penalties for improper disclosure. If such part was disclosed to any person in a foreign country or a foreign national in the U.S., the principals must not inform such person of the Secrecy Order, but instead must promptly furnish to Mail Stop L&R the following information to the extent not already furnished: date of disclosure; name and address of the disclosee; identification of such subject matter; and any authorization by a U.S. government agency to export such subject matter. If the subject matter is included in any foreign patent application or patent, this should be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not notify foreign disclosees about Secrecy Orders. Send the specified factual information to Mail Stop L&R (Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450). Include whether disclosure was authorized by a U.S. government agency and whether the subject matter appears in any foreign patent application or patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy Order duration, renewal, and continuing security obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 181, a Secrecy Order remains in effect for 1 year from its issuance and may be renewed for additional periods of not more than 1 year upon notice by a government agency that the national interest so requires. The applicant is notified of any renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expiration or failure to renew a Secrecy Order does not lessen the principals' responsibility for security if the subject matter is subject to Executive Order No. 12958, the Atomic Energy Act, or other law, unless expressly notified of declassification and cancellation of security markings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and marking of applications bearing national security markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications subject to a Secrecy Order will be deleted from USPTO image systems, converted to paper, and held with Licensing and Review. Papers marked as prescribed in Executive Orders and showing such marking applied by or at direction of a government agency are accepted in patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer any application or paper bearing words like 'Secret', 'Confidential', 'ITAR' or similar to Licensing and Review for clarification. Such applications/papers must not be placed in public records (e.g., patented files) until security markings are declassified or explained. Authorized security markings may be placed on drawings provided markings are outside illustrations and removed when declassified (37 CFR 1.84(v)). Applications filed directly with Licensing and Review without proper markings will be routed appropriately; improperly marked applications may require removal of markings or imposition of a Secrecy Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination requirements for Secrecy Order cases
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications under a Secrecy Order are examined in a secure location by examiners possessing national security clearances under the control of Licensing and Review. Secrecy Order cases are examined for patentability like other cases but will not be passed to issue; interferences or derivations are not instituted where one or more conflicting cases is classified or under Secrecy Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Secrecy Order is imposed after docketing, transfer the case to an examiner designated by Licensing and Review. Final rejections must be replied to to prevent abandonment, but appeals will not be set for hearing by the PTAB until the Secrecy Order is removed unless specifically ordered. When a Secrecy Order case is allowed, issue a notice of allowability (Form D-10) closing prosecution; amendments received after allowance are not entered or responded to until the Secrecy Order is rescinded, except amendments free from objection may be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties when national-security markings exist but no Secrecy Order
rubrics_metrics.description: When applications bear national security markings but no Secrecy Order, the examiner should require the applicant to seek imposition of a Secrecy Order or authority to cancel the markings, preferably in the first action and in any event prior to final disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to 37 CFR 5.1(d), if no Secrecy Order has issued, the Office will set a time within which the applicant must: (A) obtain a Secrecy Order; (B) declassify the application; or (C) submit evidence of a good faith effort to obtain a Secrecy Order (37 CFR 5.2(a)). A national-security classified application will not be allowed until declassified and any Secrecy Order rescinded.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a foreign filing license is required (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 5.11(a): A license from the Commissioner for Patents under 35 U.S.C. 184 is required before filing any application in a foreign country (or with a foreign or international IP authority) if the invention was made in the United States and: (1) a U.S. application on the invention has been filed less than six months prior to the date on which the foreign application is to be filed; or (2) no U.S. application on the invention has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The license also authorizes export of technical data abroad for purposes related to preparation/filing/prosecution of a foreign application and use of WIPO online services when applicable. If no license is obtained, other export regulations (ITAR, EAR, DOE) may apply. See exceptions in 37 CFR 5.11(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of unauthorized foreign filing and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 182–186: An invention subject to a Secrecy Order may be held abandoned if published/disclosed or if an application was filed in a foreign country without consent of the Commissioner of Patents; a U.S. patent may be barred or invalidated for unauthorized foreign filing without the required license. Penalties for willful violation may include fines up to $10,000 and/or imprisonment up to two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent issued despite failure to procure a license may be invalid unless the failure was through error and the patent does not disclose subject matter within the scope of section 181. The prohibitions do not apply to U.S. officers or agents acting within their authority or persons acting on written instructions/permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of a foreign filing license
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 5.15: Licenses granted under §§ 5.12–5.14 permit (subject to conditions) subsequent modifications, amendments and supplements, export and filing of duplicates and formal papers, making amendments and supporting matter, and taking actions in prosecution of the foreign application, provided such changes do not change the general nature of the invention in a manner requiring U.S. inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181. Licenses exclude adding technical data pertaining to (i) defense services/articles on the U.S. Munitions List or (ii) Restricted Data/sensitive nuclear technology governed by Atomic Energy Act and DOE regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials required to have been made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181 are eligible for a different, narrower license (paragraph (b)). Any paper filed abroad after filing that changes the general nature or involves prohibited subject matter must be separately licensed. Licenses granted for multiple U.S. applications may be combined or divided provided no prohibited subject matter is introduced and other conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content and form for foreign filing licenses (37 CFR 5.12–5.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 5.12(b) and related sections: A petition for license must include the fee under § 1.17(g), the petitioner’s address, and full instructions for delivery of the requested license when to be delivered to other than the petitioner; should be presented in letter form. If no corresponding U.S. application exists, the petition must be accompanied by a legible copy of the material for which a license is desired (37 CFR 5.13). If there is a corresponding U.S. application, the petition must identify that application by number, filing date, inventor, and title (37 CFR 5.14(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When foreign filing/application to be filed abroad contains matter not disclosed in the U.S. application, furnish a copy of the application as to be filed abroad, or identify new matter in detail if readily identifiable. Do not refer two or more U.S. applications in the same petition unless they are to be combined in the foreign filing; identify each U.S. application in separate paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting a narrow-scope license to a broad license
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants granted a license of the relatively narrow scope in 37 CFR 5.15(b) may petition under 37 CFR 5.15(c) to change the license to the broader scope of 37 CFR 5.15(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fee (§ 1.17(g)) is charged for such a petition. No such petition will be granted if the copy filed under 37 CFR 5.13 or any corresponding U.S. application was required to be made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181. If granted, the change in scope is effective as of the date of the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and recommended submission methods for license petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, a license will be granted within 3 business days from receipt of a petition filed under 37 CFR 5.12(b) in Licensing and Review if there is no national security concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to hand deliver or fax the license request directly to Licensing and Review (preferred) or submit via EFS-Web; provide a contact number or fax to which the license should be sent to avoid mailing delays. Without contact info the license will be mailed, delaying receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and evidentiary standard for retroactive (retroactive) licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 5.25: A petition for retroactive license must list each foreign country in which the unlicensed material was filed, dates of filing, and include a verified statement (oath or declaration) that (i) subject matter was not under a secrecy order when filed abroad and is not currently under a secrecy order, (ii) the license has been diligently sought after discovery of the proscribed foreign filing, and (iii) an explanation of why the material was filed abroad through error without the required license. The petition must include the required fee (§ 1.17(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The showing must be of facts, not mere allegations; include supporting documents (letters of transmittal, instructions for filing, statements by persons with personal knowledge). For petitions filed prior to Sept 16, 2012, the petition had to specify the error occurred without deceptive intent. Retroactive licenses are made retroactive only to specific acts; denials permit renewal within a set period, and final denials may be subject to § 1.181 petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with other export-control regulations (ITAR, EAR, DOE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If technical data in a patent application are exported for preparation/filing/prosecution of a foreign application without a USPTO license, the export regulations in 22 CFR parts 120–130 (ITAR), 15 CFR parts 730–774 (EAR), and 10 CFR part 810 (DOE) must be complied with unless a license is not required because a U.S. application was on file at the time of export for at least six months without a Secrecy Order under § 5.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A license from the Commissioner for Patents authorizes export for purposes related to foreign filing and may obviate separate Dept. of State approval in some cases (e.g., 22 CFR part 125) unless exporting technical data exceeding that used to support a patent application. For sensitive nuclear technology, an application filed in accordance with USPTO regulations and eligible for foreign filing is considered information available to the public for DOE regulation purposes (10 CFR 810.7). Applicants should consult the Departments of Commerce, State, and Energy as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of licenses and effects of revocation or Secrecy Order on foreign filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A license under § 5.11(a) can be revoked at any time upon written notification by the USPTO; an authorization arising from the passage of six months from the date of filing of a U.S. patent application may be revoked by the imposition of a Secrecy Order. Revocation becomes effective on the date the notice is mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation often indicates referral to defense agencies. Revocation of a filing-receipt license does not necessarily mean a petition under § 5.12(b) for a license of narrower scope will not be granted. Foreign filings occurring prior to revocation need not be abandoned, but additional filings without a license are not permitted unless six months have elapsed from the filing of any corresponding U.S. application. Once a Secrecy Order is imposed, its restrictions must immediately be observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances warranting an explicit petition under 37 CFR 5.12(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although every U.S. origin application is implicitly considered a petition for a foreign filing license, explicit petitions under 37 CFR 5.12(b) may be appropriate in cases: (A) where the filing receipt license is not granted; (B) where the filing receipt has not yet been issued (37 CFR 5.14(a) or (b)); (C) where there is no corresponding U.S. application (37 CFR 5.13); (D) where subject matter additional to that already licensed is sought to be licensed (37 CFR 5.14(c) and 5.15(e)); or (E) where expedited handling is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions under 5.14(a) or (b) and any license granted are made of record in the application file; petitions under 5.14(c) are not ordinarily made of record. The scope of any license granted will be indicated on the license itself.
